title: Running Total

story.briefing: The canopy sensors are queried constantly, always for the total across some stretch of the array. Each answer is easy; a hundred thousand answers are not.
story.success: Totals precomputed. Every query now returns in a single step.

description: Given an array of values and a list of queries, answer each query. Each query is a two-element array [l, r] asking for the sum of values from index l to index r inclusive. Return the answers in query order. Every query is within bounds, and l is never greater than r.
hints: Every query re-adds numbers that other queries have already added. Doing that work once, up front, is the whole idea.
If you know the total from the start up to each position, any range total is the difference between two of those. Getting the off-by-one right at the left edge is the hard part.
Build an array where prefix[i] is the sum of the first i values, so prefix[0] is 0. Then the sum from l to r inclusive is prefix[r + 1] minus prefix[l].
